newsitem.title: USA: Cash cheese market rolls into CME for first day.
newsitem.headline: Cash cheese market rolls into CME for first day.

text.p: The first day of trading in the wholesale cash cheese market at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange saw a total of 13 cars change hands, a brisk trade compared to the former spot market at the National Cheese Exchange in Green Bay, industry analysts said.

The first trade in spot cheddar cheese after 41 years in Green Bay came in 500-lb barrels with three contracts trading at $1.1600 per lb and five later sales in barrels to close at $1.1500, down two cents from last week's close. Five blocks traded and closed at $1.1500, down three cents from the last close.

Analysts noted that during the past three weeks, an overage of less than seven loads traded per week at the National Cheese Exchange. The industry has used these cheese sales as a benchmark for pricing other varieties of cheese and the U.S. Agriculture Department has used the change in the value of cheese from month to month to adjust the minimum raw milk price.

Part of the reason the spot market was moved to Chicago was to increase participation and its ability to manage its operations within the federal regulatory system, said Jerry Dryer, dairy and food market analyst.
"We believe this oversight will bolster confidence in the new market for cheese, therby encouraging increased trading activity," Dryer said.
Dryer also noted that to help cheese traders manage the risk that results from volatility, the CME expects to add a cheese futures contract to its menu by the end of the year.
